lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: Allocated ninety seconds per visitor. I have never once used the ninety seconds, because I have never once had two visitors, so take as long as you like.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: Callum Strand. Founder of Meridian, signatory to the Handover, and — the plaque says — a steward of the public interest.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: The plaque is two hundred years old and has been re-cast eleven times. I have the casting records. Nobody has ever asked me why a plaque needs re-casting eleven times.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: People started leaving things. Wire flowers, handwriting, a child's drawing of a machine with a face on it. I am supposed to clear the site nightly.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: I stopped about a year ago. Nobody has raised it, and I have worked out that nobody is going to, because clearing it was allocated and noticing that it has not been cleared was not.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: It came down in the spring and nothing has been allocated to put it back up.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: That is how you learn what a thing is actually worth in this century. Not what they build — anybody will build you something. What they bother to repair.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: The founding documents are behind the glass at the back, and there is a gap in them. Nineteen months in 2064 with nothing catalogued at all. I have filed about it four times, properly, through the form.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: The gap filled itself last quarter. Eleven senators, four firms and one holding company, catalogued, sourced, footnoted — to a public record I have spent nine years being unable to find.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: I did not put it there. I would very much like to know who did, and I have decided not to ask, which I am aware is the sort of decision this building runs on.

lines.speaker: memorial_docent
lines.text: Provenance, they call that. The record of who owned a thing, and when, and on whose word. It is most of my job and almost none of this building.
